Sorting by the Fiedler vector returns the ids [4, 2, 5, 1, 3], which are A, B, C, D, E: the filled order badges run straight along the path." width="100%"} Sorting nodes by their Fiedler vector entries (see `fiedler_vector()`) produces a linear ordering in which connected nodes tend to be near each other. This is spectral seriation: it is used to reorder adjacency matrices so that structure shows up as blocks along the diagonal, to lay out nodes on a line, to reduce matrix bandwidth, and to sequence items (archaeological artifacts, genome fragments) from pairwise similarities. Each connected component is ordered separately, components in order of their smallest node ID; components of one or two nodes keep ID order. Ties are broken by node ID, and since the Fiedler vector's sign is arbitrary, an ordering and its reverse are equally valid (NetworkX may return either). Matches NetworkX's `spectral_ordering()` up to these choices. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use the normalized Laplacian. Default is `False`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : All node IDs in spectral order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or empty, or has a negative weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Shuffled labels on a path come back in path order: ::: {#99e77fea .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["D", "B", "E", "A", "C"]) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in graph.spectral_ordering()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'] ``` ::: :::
